trims.template_four_points:

trims.argument:
Measured with the real navigation.first_screen, records and the kit's count (read-only harness at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/4cd2c9b9-8aca-4fd1-99bb-ff1a3f9d1698/scratchpad/trim/render.py). The four points come to 124 words (22/44/24/34), so the screen is 165 words, rendering '1–2 minutes'. Today it is 172.

What is kept:
- **The ethics:** both premises, each with its content, its role and the phrases the test needs ('fixes scope', 'alone gives order'); 'unasserted'; 'their warrant open'; no warrant binding every possible mind claimed; T8's standing as 'argued'. Nothing says the ethics derives from the condition.
- **What a receipt shows:** the claim is kept, with 'registered' (FS1) and 'Lean statement' (FS2).
- **Tests and review:** 'frozen before scoring', the failures, and the closing 'No human review yet.'
- **Links:** all eight links down.
- **The opening:** its standing as 'a first-person conviction'.
- **The earlier pass's reasons:** 'evaluation included', the glossary's gloss of the condition and 'comes to be' all stay.
- **The fixed parts:** no names, all four points, every field as written. The title, nav, banner and time line are untouched. The template's leading comment stands, and it is still true: the screen is still over, by what cannot be cut.

**Why 150 cannot be reached.** For 150 the four points must be 109 words or fewer. Exactly 110 renders 151, because the time line then goes from 'a minute' to '1–2 minutes'. I cut everything that is on no must-stay list:
- the three reading times, 9 words;
- 'evaluation included', 2 words.

That variant renders at 113 words and a 154-word screen (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/4cd2c9b9-8aca-4fd1-99bb-ff1a3f9d1698/scratchpad/trim/floor.md). The 113 words left are all must-stay:
- point 1, 20 words: what the theory is, and 'not assumed good';
- point 2, 44 words, as listed above;
- point 3, 15 words: the four links and the opening's standing;
- point 4, 34 words: the receipt, the frozen tests, the failures and the review.

The last 4 words could only come from items like 'whose losses count' (what scope means) or 'their warrant open'.

I also kept the times and 'evaluation included', so the proposal is 165, not 154:
- **The times:** READING-BUDGETS says what brings this screen within budget is 'a screen naming each layer with its time'. The one page and the overview do not yet state their own times at their tops, so cutting the times to meet the budget would defeat what the budget is for.
- **'Evaluation included':** the earlier pass kept it because values take shape inside the account, as AGENTS and ONE-PAGE say.

So amendment 1 applies. The landing's study section should record 165, 15 over. It should also name the times as part of the excess, since the comment's list leaves them out.

The banner is unchanged. It is what says the work is not finalized, which is what Ren's words of 31 October bear on. Outside the strategy, only the banner (18 words) and the nav bar (14) remain as places to save words.

trims.argument:
Total: 149 words, from the real navigation.first_screen run on the proposed file in a scratch root with the live records. The same harness gives 172 for today's file. A screen of exactly 150 cannot render. Below 150 the time field reads 'a minute' (2 words), and at 150 it flips to '1–2 minutes' (3 words), which makes 151. So 'at most 150' really means at most 149, or at most 145 words outside the time line. The proposal hits that limit exactly, with no slack: one added word anywhere makes 151.

So 150 is reachable without a loss, but only through the status line. The four points alone can lose just 6 words without loss, which gives 166. Everything else in them is on the must-stay list.

Items the screen may never lose, and where each sits:
- Title and navigation (lines 1 and 5). They are generated for every page and are not this file's to cut.
- The status: ongoing, unfinished (banner).
- The reading time where the layer begins (the time line; item 6).
- Point 1:
  - 'An account' and 'anything'.
  - 'evaluation included': a reason the tightening pass kept, AGENTS's relational basis for fact/value.
  - 'comes to be, lasts, changes and passes away': the opening's own words. Rewording them would restate the opening in other words, and 'arises' is wrong.
  - 'within one relational unfolding'.
  - 'not assumed good': not claimed.
- Point 2:
  - The two premises (link), 'unasserted' (standing) and 'warrant open' (not claimed).
  - The condition with its glossary gloss and its quantifier.
  - 'fixes scope, whose losses count': the role. The gloss guards FS5's misreading of 'life's way'.
  - C with its gloss and 'alone gives order' (FS4; 'orders' could be read as commands).
  - The T8 link and 'Thesis' (standing).
  - 'this ethics', not 'it', which could be read as C.
  - 'claiming no verdict binding every possible mind': withholding the claim, not denying it, so nothing against the opening.
- Point 3:
  - 'Start with', the four links and the three time fields.
  - 'a first-person conviction': the opening's standing, and the only mark on a screen that names no one that the opening is in a different voice.
  - 'with notes' after the time.
- Point 4:
  - 'Recorded' (stale receipts), 'credit' (FS1) and the count fields (amendment 3).
  - 'registered' (the denominator is the register).
  - What a receipt shows (FS2).
  - 'frozen before scoring' (FS8), 'some passed, some failed' (failures with their standing), and 'No human review yet.' as the last words.

Every cut word carries none of these. All 8 link targets and all 7 fields are byte-identical to today's. No new term or claim is added, and no person or AI is named. Every reason the tightening pass gave still holds. That pass worked inside the block, where the never-cut content does not fit beside a frame of 36 words. The room comes from the status line, which it never touched; at 2 words the frame takes 20. The template's leading comment stays except for one sentence: 'is over the gate's 150 words … records the excess' would become false, and a correction is never held back. It now says the screen is within 150, that the title, navigation and status line count toward it, and that the study section records the count.

If the coordinator later rules out 'evaluation included', which the tightening pass named as discretionary, the screen gets two words of slack (147).

losses: What is not claimed (on the never-cut list in amendment 1 and READING-BUDGETS; required by AGENTS) is weakened in point 2. Today's wording is T8's own sentence ('claiming no verdict binding every possible mind'; 07 T8: 'No verdict binding every possible mind is claimed'). The earlier pass chose it because it withholds the claim rather than denying it (tighten.json, final findings). The trim reads 'their warrant open, none binding every possible mind claimed'. That is an absolute construction with no 'with' and its participle at the very end, so the first parse a reader reaches is 'none binding every possible mind', which is a denial. That is the misreading the earlier pass fixed, and under the opening's 'basis of all ethics, for all beings, in all universes' a denial reads as the screen contradicting the opening. The antecedent of 'none' is also unclear. If it is 'two unasserted premises', the grammar would need 'neither', and the withheld claim becomes one about premises binding minds, not about the verdict. If it is 'warrant', a mass noun, it can only be read as 'no warrant'. T8's verdict clause is then covered only by inference ('a verdict binding every mind would need such a warrant'), not stated.

Each claim's standing (amendment 1), in the one sense GLOSSARY gives: 'standing | what kind of claim a statement is: definition, theorem with its base, conditional, calibration, thesis, assessment, reading, open'. A reader who follows 'argued as life's way' is not told which thesis to read.

Plausible, low: the trim weakens the guard behind FS5's resolution. In the trim, 'argued as life's way' comes first, as an apposition to 'Its ethics', before the scope is stated, so the order that refutation relied on is reversed. T8's own guard ('For life says whose way it is, not whose losses count') is not on the screen.
errors: The template's leading comment is kept word for word, and the trimmer calls it 'still true'. It says the screen is over 150 'by what amendment 1 ... does not let a layer cut' and by what the review and the coordinator asked to keep. The trim's 'none binding every possible mind claimed' is a compressed paraphrase that drops both 'with' and 'warrant'.

losses: What is not claimed, verdict form (never cut, amendment 1). The trim deletes T8's own withholding, 'claiming no verdict binding every possible mind', and puts 'none binding every possible mind claimed' after the premises' warrant. The trim argues that 'a verdict binding every mind would need such a warrant'. The account itself separates the two. 07 §8 T8 says 'that their shared verdict binds those whose own line runs through life, is the thesis. No verdict binding every possible mind is claimed', while P2, P4 and a reason for C stay open. So T8 argues a binding verdict, scoped to life, with the premises' warrant open, and withholding the warrant does not cover withholding the verdict. The opening's notes give the two separately: note 6, 'No warrant binding every possible mind is claimed', and note 8, 'Open, and offered for life: no verdict binding every possible mind is claimed'. The overview's T8 row also says 'no verdict binding every possible mind is claimed'. After the trim, only the warrant form is left on the screen.

The withholding can be read as a denial. The phrase starts with the negative quantifier and puts 'claimed' last: 'none binding every possible mind ... claimed'. On a first pass this reads as 'none binds every possible mind'. The earlier pass rejected 'not as binding every possible mind' for exactly this reason (tighten.json, judge 1 and finding 2 of the final). A denial goes beyond 07 Open (r-universal-practical-warrant: 'these do not show that none exists'). The old construction put the verb first ('claiming no verdict ...'), so no garden path arose.

The antecedent of 'none' is ambiguous. It can be 'two unasserted premises', though for two English would say 'neither'. It can also be 'warrant'. On the premises reading the screen says premises bind minds. In the account it is a warrant (AGENTS, 07 Open, 08 §12) or a verdict (T8) that binds, never a premise. The second ambiguity is the one-sense issue.

The label 'Thesis' leaves the screen with 'T8'. verdicts.notes:
How it was measured: a read-only render of the proposed template through the real navigation.first_screen and the records, with the template's leading comment kept and the kit's measure_layers count. The proposal is 165 words (title, nav and banner 36; time line 5; points 22/44/24/34), against 172 today. Scratch files are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/4cd2c9b9-8aca-4fd1-99bb-ff1a3f9d1698/scratchpad/trim/acc/.

What the diff touches: only the words of point 2 and point 4. All seven fields and all eight link targets are byte-identical. The title, nav, banner, time line, points 1 and 3, 'No human review yet.' and the no-names rule are unchanged.

What checks out:
- Both premises are named with their roles ('fixes scope, whose losses count'; 'alone gives order', as GLOSSARY has it), with 'unasserted' and 'their warrant open'.
- Nothing says the ethics derives from the condition.
- 'Argued' is T8's Standing in 07 §8 and 08 §9.
- Placing 'argued' on 'Its ethics' before C is named removes the reading of 'it' as C, as the trim says.
- What a receipt shows is untouched.
- 'Tests frozen before scoring' is kept, and no partitive brings back the 'only some tests were frozen' reading.
- The banner stays consistent with Ren's 31 October words ('not the finalized version').

Recommended fix, which keeps most of the saving: restore T8's verdict wording as a participle on the ethics and drop the 'none' clause. Point 2 becomes: '**Its ethics**, [argued as life's way](../../theories/becoming/chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#theses), claiming no verdict binding every possible mind, rests on [two unasserted premises](../../theories/becoming/chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#scope-and-order), their warrant open: the continuation condition (...) fixes scope, whose losses count; C (...) alone gives order.' Rendered, that is 45 words in point 2 and 166 on the screen (fix-verdict-noand.md). It brings back T8's withholding in its own words, a verb first and a withholding rather than a denial, and loses no other gain.

In today's wording the number agreement (singular 'statement', plural 'they') leaves 'they' only one antecedent, the premises. In the plural form 'these' can refer either to the premises or to the Lean statements. If it refers to the statements, the clause says receipts do not show that the Lean statements hold. In the account's vocabulary 'goes on' is a term (GLOSSARY: goes on, 延). Read of the unfolding, it would assert an unconditional 'always' that the opening's own law qualifies: 'Whatever is closed ... cannot go on forever without coming to rest'. (b) 'Revised' goes. 'Unfinished' says more remains to do. It does not say that what is already stated, proofs and readings included, may change. Ren's 31 October words carry both: 'we still have more to do, so this is not the finalized version', after 'i don't think it is good enough'.
